**MS-303 — "Move to next OOS from OOS page (just some < and > arrows)"**

One deliverable, small. The Order of Service editor is one page (`service-builder.html?date=YYYY-MM-DD`), and Services already treats Sundays as pure arithmetic — every week from July 2023 to two years out, document or not. So "next" is just +7 days. No query needed.

It reads **sharp, not trivial**. The title names the change exactly, but the page it lands on has two things that bite a naive build:

1. **It autosaves and guards the exit.** Three seconds after your last edit it writes, and there's a `beforeunload` handler that pops the browser's "Leave site?" box while you're dirty. Wire an arrow to a plain page navigation and you get that dialog on every click — during the guide-writing evening, which is exactly when someone clicks through eight Sundays in a row.
2. **The box lock follows you.** Only one person can sit in a hymn slot at a time, and presence is keyed to which page and which Sunday. Move dates without re-keying it and you appear parked on a Sunday you left, holding a box nobody can take.

There's also a real cost call: the page reloads the whole people directory and hymn index on open, so a full page nav per arrow is one line of code but slow, while swapping in place is snappier and more work.

**I'd take this to `/grill-with-docs`** — short, ~10 minutes. Four things to settle: does the arrow flush the pending save and go, does it reload the page or swap in place, where do the arrows stop, and does the URL change so back/refresh work. Everything else I can read out of the code.

**Placement:** the only open epics are "Roles & Serving Scheduler" and "Phase 1 (Legacy)" — neither fits. I'd call this standalone.

## (c) Claimed but the implementation looks wrong

**1. "Starting on the Roles tab and pressing an arrow lands on the Roles tab of the next Sunday."**
It lands there empty. `service-builder.js:801` restores the tab straight after `load()`, but the people list isn't fetched until `loadPeopleRegistry()` at line 806. The Roles panel's `x-data="eventDetailPage({ ..., people: peopleRegistry })"` (`service-builder.html:1206`) is evaluated once, when Alpine flushes during the very next `await` — and line 845 *reassigns* `this.peopleRegistry`, so the panel holds the initial `[]` for good. Arriving by arrow gives a Roles tab you can't put anyone into; tapping the tab by hand is fine. Move the restore below `loadPeopleRegistry()`.

**2. "Hovering an arrow names the Sunday it leads to; a disabled one says there is none."**
The name is a `title` on a `disabled` button (`service-builder.html:227`, `:disabled` + `:title`). Chrome and Firefox don't show `title` tooltips on disabled controls, and the `aria-label` is unreachable too since a disabled button takes no focus. The *enabled* half works; the disabled half almost certainly doesn't.

**3. "If that save fails, the page does not move and the existing save error is shown."**
Holds for the ordinary failure (`save(true)` alerts, returns false). But if `save` ever throws, `stepService` (`service-builder.js:712-725`) has no `try/finally`, so `stepping` stays `true` and *both* arrows are dead until reload. `service-step.test.js` explicitly pins the throwing case, yet the only caller doesn't honour it.

**4. "no browser 'leave site?' prompt appears."**
Type during the in-flight save and `committed && this.isDirty` re-arms (line 1574); `beforeunload` at line 817 then fires anyway and that edit is lost. Narrow, but real. Relatedly, the arrow's `save(true)` has no `this.saving` guard, so it can run a second batch alongside a live autosave.
